evidence.title: Bella Sidney Woolf
evidence.text: Bella Sidney Woolf OBE (1877–1960) was an English author, sister of author Leonard Woolf and first married to Robert Heath Lock, and in her second marriage to Hong Kong colonial secretary and colonial Ceylonese administrator Tom Southorn.

evidence.title: Thomas Southorn
evidence.text: Sir Wilfrid Thomas Southorn( 4 August 1879 – 15 March 1957)( Chinese Translated Name: 修頓, Old Translated Name: 蕭敦), known as Tom, was a British colonial administrator, spending the large part of career in Ceylon( now Sri Lanka).

evidence.title: Thomas Southorn
evidence.text: He was the Colonial Secretary of Hong Kong from 1925 – 1936 and served as Acting Administrator of the colony from February to March 1930 and from May to September 1935, and then in November the same year, basically at either end of the tenure of Sir William Peel as Governor.

evidence.title: Thomas Southorn
evidence.text: His official( summer) residence was Mountain Lodge.

evidence.title: Thomas Southorn
evidence.text: In 1921 he married author Bella Sidney Woolf( 1877 – 1960), whom he met through her( later) more famous brother Leonard Woolf, when the two men were colleagues in Ceylon.

evidence.title: Thomas Southorn
evidence.text: In 1904, then a humble' Office Assistant', Southorn had met Leonard Woolf on his arrival in Ceylon from England.

evidence.title: Thomas Southorn
evidence.text: In 1936, he was made Governor of The Gambia, notably describing the colony as" a geographical and economic absurdity".

evidence.title: Sidney Woolf
evidence.text: Sidney Woolf (16 June 1837 – September, 1918) was an English pottery manufacturer and a Liberal Party politician who sat in the House of Commons from 1880 to 1885.
